title: Lifecycle once
summary: xtpd owns every stage of every service's life on the node: open, accept, keepalive, half-close, close and abort; key refresh, rotation and revocation; route health and failover between L2, L3 and L4; admission against the operating state; receipts for every open, refusal and close; and its own start and stop, including the firewall set and the emergency files. systemd starts it once at boot.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: No application re-implements session, key, route or firewall lifecycle
No TCP listener remains on an MU once xtpd carries SSH

provenance.claim: XTP sessions: one context, both directions, per-direction close, one listener socket for all sessions
Per-service keys, LDAP first then a mode-600 key file; protected FIRST checked before any state

qualification_boundaries.status: dev1 built: packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev1 (Claude (Opus 5.5), 24 Nov 2026) - registrations, peerages and keys from files, unix-socket OPEN with descriptor passing, exec hooks, the fence, receipts through oorexx_logging
qualification_boundaries.field: tested on loopback only (two daemons, real OpenSSH over UDP and raw IP 36); not field-tested; LDAP inputs, operating states, emergency files and the role bootstrap are not built
